classification.difficultyReason: One explanation. The student must see that 2/3 is a never-ending recurring decimal, that the display is cut at 9 decimal places, and that the next digit 6 is at least 5, so the last 6 rounds up to 7. This links recurring decimals to the critical-digit rounding rule with no scaffolding, but it is a single short step. It is a little harder than the open-ended classification in p14-q7 and easier than the multi-part conversion and explanation in p13-q5.

content.prompt: A calculator displays $2\div3$ as $0.666\,666\,667$. Explain why the last digit is $7$ when every other digit is $6$.

answer.short: $2\div3=0.666\ldots$ is a recurring decimal, so it never ends. The calculator shows 9 decimal places and rounds. The next digit is $6$, which is 5 or more, so the last digit is rounded up from $6$ to $7$.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}2\div3&=0.666\,666\,666\,6\ldots\\\text{9 decimal places:}&\quad 0.666\,666\,666\,|\,6\ldots\\\text{next digit is }6\ge5&\Rightarrow\text{round up}\\&\approx0.666\,666\,667\end{align*}$$The decimal never ends, so the display is rounded. The final $6$ is rounded up to $7$.
